questions.q: Does spoken-speech transfer match the imagined-speech baseline, and what exactly was compared?
questions.answer: The authors report 26.8% mean accuracy (SD 2.0) for full spoken-speech transfer versus 30.5% (SD 4.9) for imagined-speech 10-fold cross-validation, with p = 0.0983 and chi-square = 4.64. They describe the result as comparable, but report no equivalence test; the conditions differ because one uses spoken-speech training and the other imagined-speech training.

questions.q: How strong is the visual-imagery comparison as evidence that imagined speech is more related to spoken speech?
questions.answer: The visual-imagery baseline is 31.8% (SD 4.1) and full spoken-speech transfer is 26.3% (SD 2.4), with p = 0.022 and chi-square = 7.64. The authors use this contrast alongside the non-significant imagined-speech comparison to infer a closer relation, but it remains a comparison across paradigms rather than direct evidence of a shared mechanism.

questions.q: Which reported protocol details and omissions most constrain reproduction and interpretation?
questions.answer: The paper specifies a five-class task, seven-subject datasets, a random 90/10 imagined-speech split in 10-fold cross-validation, CSP/SVM, and a few-trial model trained with 10 spoken trials per class. It does not report the selected class identities, seed/repeats, separate validation or selection data, preprocessing/normalization, chance comparison, full trial counts, or a held-out-subject/session protocol.
